name: Texel Size Adaptation and Primitive Management
definition: A routine that adapts the resolution of texture maps (texel size) and manages the number of 3D Gaussian primitives based on quantile error thresholds, running periodically during training to balance model capacity and appearance quality.
summary: Texel Size Adaptation and Primitive Management is a training-time optimization that dynamically adjusts per-primitive texture resolution and primitive counts using quantile-based error thresholds to balance model capacity and appearance quality.
